svg.aria-label: How to write 吗: 6 strokes · 5 pen lifts · 11 movements
svg.title: Writing 吗
svg.desc: 11 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 吗 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 吗.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E5%90%97.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 吗. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses: its left vertical, its joined top and right sides, and its closing bottom horizontal, all inside the upper-left third of the square. Medians 4–6 then draw 马: a horizontal that turns down at the right, a long stroke that turns twice and hooks, and a wide finishing horizontal that runs almost the full width of the character and is the widest stroke in it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, directions, the two joined corners and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
